note: Great shot of these blooming by Alaina, one of our high school volunteers! The mass planting outside the office is at times unruly, so we enjoy them now while we can.
quick_hits: Look between the red bracts: the slim orange tubes with dark tips are the actual flowers, and on this heliconia they are half the show.
Each flower opens just before dawn and has stopped making nectar by early afternoon.
In Brazil a skipper butterfly pollinates it before sunrise, alongside hummingbirds and an orchid bee.

note: Unexpected Helping Hand. Photographer Helen Lewis spotted something remarkable: a Northern Cardinal feeding a young Northern Mockingbird chick. A wonderful little moment of unexpected care, caught right here at the park.
quick_hits: Males are bright red with a pointed crest and black face mask; females are warm buff-brown with red tinges. Both carry the same stout orange-red bill.
Both sexes sing. In many North American songbirds only the male does.
That heavy conical bill is a seed-cracker, opening tough seeds many birds cannot manage.

note: A cornsnake surprised us by jumping out from our pond plants into the water! Harmless, handsome, and colorful!
Our team planted a new tree in September to replace the fallen baobab from the storms of past years. We also lost a rainbow eucalyptus near the cactus garden, so this is a welcome back of sorts!
quick_hits: The bark peels away in strips. The fresh bark underneath is bright green, and it darkens through blues, purples and oranges as it ages.
Unlike most eucalyptus, it comes from rainforest, not dry Australian bush.
On Maui, a roadside grove of these trees is one of the famous stops on the Road to Hana.
